title: Build the Mass
objective: Lift a copy of the floor plate, twist it, and loft between the two into a closed tower mass.
learn: Vectors and transforms (Move, Rotate), then turning profiles into a solid with Loft and Cap Holes.

nodes.need: a vector pointing straight up, as long as the Height slider
nodes.hint: Vector › Vector. Up is the Z axis, and the factor sets the length.
nodes.correct: Unit Z makes a vector pointing up the Z axis. Its Factor is the Height slider, so the vector is exactly as tall as the tower.

wrong.unitX: Unit X points sideways along X — the top plate has to go up.
wrong.constructPoint: Construct Point makes a location. Move needs a direction and distance: a vector.
wrong.amplitude: Amplitude resizes an existing vector, but there is no vector yet.
wrong.*: This slot needs a vector pointing straight up.

nodes.need: a transform that lifts the top copy along the vector
nodes.hint: Transform › Euclidean. Geometry in, Motion vector in.
nodes.correct: Move translates geometry along a vector. The top copy of the plate is lifted to the full height of the tower.

wrong.rotate: Rotate turns geometry in place — you'll need it next, but first the plate has to go up.
wrong.scale: Scale resizes around a point; the plate would stay on the ground.
wrong.extrude: Extrude would push the plate straight up into a prism — no chance to twist the top.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that shifts geometry along a vector.

nodes.need: a transform that twists the lifted plate by an angle
nodes.correct: Rotate turns the lifted plate around the world Z axis. This Rotate has Degrees switched on (right-click the A input), so the Twist slider reads 0–90°.

wrong.move: Move is already in place. Now the top needs to turn, not shift.
wrong.mirror: Mirror flips the plate across a plane — a jump, not a gradual twist.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that turns geometry by an angle.

nodes.need: a component that skins a surface between the base and the twisted top
nodes.hint: Surface › Freeform. It takes a list of section curves.
nodes.correct: Loft skins a surface through the section curves in order — base plate, then twisted top. Both wires go into the same C input, which merges them into one list.

wrong.extrude: Extrude pushes one curve along a vector; it can't connect two different profiles.
wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces only fills flat outlines — it would give two separate floor discs.
wrong.pipe: Pipe wraps a tube around a curve.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that skins a surface between section curves.

nodes.need: a component that closes the open top and bottom of the loft
nodes.hint: Surface › Util. The loft is a tube with two planar openings.
nodes.correct: Cap Holes fills the planar openings at the top and bottom, turning the lofted tube into a closed solid mass.

wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces would make loose discs, not join them to the loft into one solid.
wrong.loft: Loft is already making the side surface.
wrong.extrude: Extrude would add more geometry instead of closing the existing openings.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that closes the loft's openings.

check.prompt: Which input of Move takes the Unit Z vector?
check.hint: G = geometry to move, T = the motion vector.
check.correct: T is the motion. Until it was connected, Move used its default of 10 units up — now the top sits at the full Height.

wrong.G: G is the geometry to move — the top copy of the plate is already plugged in there.
wrong.*: That input isn't the motion vector.

check.prompt: The Twist slider should drive which input of Rotate?
check.hint: G = geometry, A = angle, P = plane to rotate around.
check.correct: A is the angle. Until it was connected, Rotate used its default (90°); now the Twist slider controls it.

wrong.G: G is the geometry — the lifted plate is already connected.
wrong.P: P is the rotation plane. Left empty it's World XY, which spins the plate around the tower's axis — exactly what we want.
